title: Unified resumable rerank + batching ergonomics across SDKs
creator: Ava Patel
description: Add a unified, ergonomic pattern for paginated/batched embeddings + rerank requests across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Deliver a ResumableBatchIterator abstraction that supports streaming responses, deterministic rerank ordering, configurable retry/backoff strategies, and low-memory client-side buffering so long-running rerank jobs (tens of thousands of items) can run reliably without OOM or lost order. Provide canonical examples and integration tests that demonstrate parity between SDKs and document migration from current cursor-based helpers.
acceptance_criteria: ResumableBatchIterator implemented in Python, TypeScript, and Go with matching API surface and examples
End-to-end examples show identical rerank output ordering across languages for same inputs (deterministic seed in integration tests)
Streaming ergonomics: client can process and early-cancel without leaking goroutines/threads or leaving sockets open
Retry/backoff profiles configurable per-call and persisted across iterator resumption
Benchmarks show memory usage remains O(batch_size) for 100k items and latency overhead <= 12% compared to non-resumable fast-path
Docs and migration guide published in SDK docs and linked from Console quickstarts
tasks: Spec API surface and examples (Python/TS/Go) - deliver design doc
Prototype Python iterator with streaming + resumable state snapshot
Implement TypeScript async iterator + stream-friendly cancel token
Implement Go channel-based iterator with explicit Close and Resume APIs
Add deterministic ordering tests and seeded integration harness
Add unit + e2e tests for retry/backoff and resume semantics
Create docs, migration guide, and copy examples into repo templates
Run benchmarks and update Optimize recommendations based on results
implementation_notes: Prefer explicit small API surface: .next(batchSize) for synchronous clients and async iteration for idiomatic TS/Python
Resume state should include: last-processed-offset, partial-batch-buffer (if any), and retry-window token; encode as base64 JSON for portability
Avoid hidden goroutine/promise leaks by requiring explicit Close()/cancel() on long-lived streaming handles

Server-side support exists for cursor+streaming but current behavior may reorder items when batching and KV cache hits occur; we'll add a server-side stable-seq header to guarantee deterministic order during resume
Backoff defaults: jittered exponential (base=200ms, max=5s) with configurable max_attempts; surface hooks for custom RetryPolicy implementation
Make embeddings batching cooperative with rerank scoring so clients can opt into prefetching embedding batches vs streaming-only pipelines
